official.deadline_note: Official T&C FAQ: 'Applicants who wish to apply for the SUSS Research Scholarship should submit their PhD application by the deadlines below' - by 28 February for the July semester and by 31 August for the next January semester. Shortlisted applicants are notified to attend an interview by end May for the July semester and end November for the January semester. No standalone scholarship deadline exists.
official.application_cycle: Semester intakes (July and January); T&C FAQ published 12 Dec 2025 lists 28 February (July semester) and 31 August (January semester) as the application cut-offs
official.status_note: Official pages publish the award as currently offered; eligible applicants to the three programmes are evaluated on a merit basis during their admissions interviews, and potential applicants are identified and nominated as part of the interview process. Terms and Conditions updated 12 Dec 2025.
official.tuition_coverage_note: For part-time students, the scholarship covers the tuition fee (excludes annual miscellaneous fees). For full-time students, the scholarship covers the tuition fees (exclude annual miscellaneous fees) and a monthly stipend. Government-subsidised tuition fees are available to eligible Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents; International Students are eligible for the subsidy only if awarded the SUSS Research Scholarship.
benefits: Full-time students: tuition fees (excluding annual miscellaneous fees) plus a monthly stipend - PhD: S$4,300 (Singapore Citizen), S$3,900 (Permanent Resident), S$3,500 (International Student)
Full-time Master of Applied Research in Social Sciences monthly stipend: S$3,800 (Singapore Citizen), S$3,000 (Permanent Resident), S$2,900 (International Student)
CPF will be given on top of the stipend amounts for Singapore Citizens
Part-time students: tuition fee only (excludes annual miscellaneous fees), no stipend
International Students are eligible for the government tuition subsidy only if awarded the SUSS Research Scholarship
No service bond attached to the scholarship
eligibility: Applicant seeking admission to one of the three Postgraduate by Research programmes: Doctor of Philosophy (Office of Graduate Studies), Doctor of Philosophy (Gerontology) (S R Nathan School of Human Development), or Master of Applied Research in Social Sciences (School of Humanities and Behavioural Sciences)
Outstanding academic results - at least a 2nd Upper Class Honours Degree from a reputable university or equivalent qualifications

Demonstrated academic excellence in social sciences; research topic related to SUSS's Research Focus (education, adult learning, lifelong learning; workplace innovation, social innovation, community engagement; business and financial innovation; Environmental, Social and Governance related topics)
Research proposals relevant to the social services sector, with a clearly identified industry collaborator and likely cash and/or in-kind industry support, will be prioritised
Open for both full-time and part-time study
requirements: Recipients shall maintain a cumulative grade point average (CGPA) of at least 3.8 in every semester
Full-time scholarship recipients are not allowed to participate in any occupation or business during the programme, unless prior written approval of SUSS has been obtained

International Students on scholarship shall fulfil Graduate Assistantship Programme (GAP) requirements (teaching/research assistance or other relevant developmental assignments) with no remuneration: MRESS part-time 78 hours / full-time 156 hours; PhD part-time 208 hours / full-time 416 hours
Recipients must sit for all examinations, complete the programme within the prescribed time and conform to programme regulations
The scholarship may not be held concurrently with any other award without prior approval of SUSS
Deferment of the scholarship is not allowed; there is no service bond
documents: PhD or Master of Applied Research in Social Sciences programme application submitted by the intake deadline (28 February for July semester; 31 August for January semester)
Research Proposal Template application form with interest in the SUSS Research Scholarship indicated
Academic transcripts and degree evidence of at least a 2nd Upper Class Honours Degree from a reputable university or equivalent qualifications
For prioritised proposals: documentation of industry support such as MOA/MOU or Letter of Support
selection_criteria: Eligible applicants to the three programmes are evaluated on a merit basis during their admissions interviews
Potential applicants for the scholarship are identified and nominated as part of the interview process
Priority given to proposals relevant to the social services sector with a clearly identified industry collaborator and likely cash and/or in-kind industry support

Shortlisted applicants are notified to attend an interview by end May for the July semester and end November for the January semester; SUSS notifies nominated applicants via email to attend a panel interview
The decision of the Student Awards Committee of SUSS is final and binding; no reasons are given for non-selection and no appeals are entertained
coverage: Tuition fees (excludes annual miscellaneous fees) for both full-time and part-time students
Monthly stipend for full-time students only: PhD S$4,300 / S$3,900 / S$3,500 and MRESS S$3,800 / S$3,000 / S$2,900 by Singapore Citizen / Permanent Resident / International Student
CPF contributions on top of the stipend for Singapore Citizens
Annual miscellaneous fees are explicitly excluded from coverage
application_method: Submit the PhD (or MRESS) programme application by the published intake deadline - by 28 February for the July semester, by 31 August for the next January semester
Indicate interest in the SUSS Research Scholarship in the Research Proposal Template application form
Be evaluated on merit during the programme's admissions interview; nomination happens within the interview process
Nominated applicants receive an email invitation to attend a panel interview for the scholarship (shortlists notified by end May for July semester, end November for January semester)
official.application_route: No separate scholarship form - apply for admission to one of the three eligible postgraduate research programmes, flag scholarship interest in the Research Proposal Template, and await nomination and the panel interview
official.study_mode: Full-time or part-time (monthly stipend for full-time students only; part-time students receive tuition fee coverage only)
official.citizenship_residency: Open to all nationalities; stipend tier depends on citizenship status - Singapore Citizen, Permanent Resident, or International Student
official.international_eligibility: Yes - open to all nationalities; International Students receive the International Student stipend tier and must fulfil the unpaid Graduate Assistantship Programme (GAP) requirement
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Research topic must relate to SUSS's Research Focus; proposals relevant to the social services sector with a clearly identified industry collaborator and likely cash and/or in-kind industry support are prioritised
official.research_requirement: Yes - a research proposal related to SUSS's Research Focus is required, indicated in the Research Proposal Template application form
official.duration: Maximum of four (4) years for PhD programmes and two (2) years for the Master of Applied Research in Social Sciences
official.description: The SUSS Research Scholarship aims to support applicants who have demonstrated academic excellence in social sciences and whose proposed research aligns with the research focus of the Singapore University of Social Sciences and the expertise of its faculty. For full-time students it covers tuition fees (excluding annual miscellaneous fees) and pays a monthly stipend that varies by programme and citizenship status; part-time students receive tuition fee coverage only.
official.program_type: Research scholarship for postgraduate research programmes (PhD, PhD Gerontology, Master of Applied Research in Social Sciences)

travel_coverage - no travel or installation allowance is published

deadline years - the official T&C FAQ states the cut-offs as '28 February' and '31 August' without printing the year
verification.notes: Stipend matrix (S$4,300/S$3,900/S$3,500 PhD; S$3,800/S$3,000/S$2,900 MRESS), tuition/miscellaneous-fee exclusion, tenure, GAP hours, CGPA 3.8 rule and the 28 February / 31 August application cut-offs were cross-checked between the official SUSS scholarship page and the official Terms & Conditions PDF (updated 12 Dec 2025) on suss.edu.sg; both figures agree and no aggregator sources were used.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no standalone scholarship form: you apply to the PhD or MRESS programme and flag your interest inside the Research Proposal Template, then get nominated during the admissions interview, so your real deadline is the programme intake cut-off - 28 February for July, 31 August for January. Full-time study is where the money is: S$3,500-S$4,300 a month for a PhD (S$2,900-S$3,800 for MRESS, depending on citizenship) plus tuition, while part-time recipients get tuition only. You must still fund the annual miscellaneous fees yourself, hold a CGPA of 3.8 every semester, and international scholars clock up to 416 unpaid GAP hours for a full-time PhD - plan finances and time around that.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Social-science researchers with at least a 2nd Upper Class Honours degree whose topic maps onto SUSS's Research Focus, especially social-services-sector proposals that already have an industry collaborator lined up.
application_readiness_checklist: Anchor the research proposal in one named SUSS Research Focus area (education/lifelong learning, workplace or social innovation, business and financial innovation, or ESG) rather than a generic topic
Line up the industry collaborator and document the expected cash or in-kind support (MOA/MOU or letter of support) - these are the proposals the official FAQ says get priority
Lodge the PhD application by 28 February (July intake) or 31 August (January intake) and explicitly indicate scholarship interest in the Research Proposal Template
Prepare for the scholarship panel interview that follows nomination; shortlists are notified by end May (July semester) or end November (January semester)
Budget for annual miscellaneous fees, Singapore living costs beyond the stipend, and - for international students - up to 156 (MRESS full-time) or 416 (PhD full-time) unpaid GAP hours
common_rejection_risks: A proposal that does not map onto a published SUSS Research Focus area - alignment with faculty expertise is an explicit eligibility rule, not a nice-to-have
Missing the programme intake deadline, because nomination only happens inside a live admissions round
No identifiable industry collaborator or support evidence despite priority being explicitly given to social-services-sector proposals with such support
Holding or accepting another concurrent award without prior SUSS approval, which the terms prohibit
Assuming full coverage - annual miscellaneous fees are excluded and the stipend is a fixed monthly amount, not a guarantee of living costs
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Annual miscellaneous fees are explicitly excluded, and the scholarship publishes no travel, installation or insurance allowance - airfare to Singapore, visa/Student's Pass costs, insurance, and living costs beyond the fixed monthly stipend come out of your own pocket.
document_audit: The Research Proposal Template is the only stated channel for signalling scholarship interest - a programme application without it will not be considered for the award

If your degree is not labelled '2nd Upper Class Honours', prepare transcripts plus a grading-scale/equivalence explanation, since the bar is 'at least a 2nd Upper Class Honours Degree from a reputable university or equivalent qualifications'
Industry support should be evidenced in writing (MOA/MOU or letter of support), as these are the named examples of qualifying cash/in-kind support
International applicants should be ready for the unpaid GAP assignment structure - 156 hours (MRESS full-time) or 416 hours (PhD full-time) - with no remuneration for those hours
alerts: The 31 August cut-off for the January intake and the 28 February cut-off for the July intake are the only published dates; there is no separate scholarship deadline to plan around
Switching from full-time to part-time study stops the monthly stipend immediately, and international students must also notify ICA to cancel their student pass
No deferment is allowed once awarded and there is no bond, but the Student Awards Committee decision is final with no appeals - treat the panel interview as your one shot

Do not confuse this with the separate SUSS PhD Scholarship (full-time PhD programmes only, stipend S$2,200-S$3,300 by stage and citizenship, covers miscellaneous fees) - they have different value structures and eligibility
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Programme application first with the Research Proposal Template and scholarship interest flagged, merit screening at the admissions interview, email nomination to the scholarship panel interview, then a final Student Awards Committee decision.
